name: Slagside Rivet-Crown Face Shield
description:
Hammered from salvaged industrial press plates and bent into rough face coverage, the Rivet-Crown is a Shelf staple — ugly, functional, and unmistakably hand-made. Mismatched rivet heads hold overlapping panels of grey and rust-orange scrap steel, with a scratched polycarbonate visor strip salvaged from a defunct transit shelter. The forehead brace is wrapped in friction tape over reclaimed foam padding.

No two are identical. Chin straps are knotted cord or stripped wire depending on the maker's day. Acid-rain pitting marks every surface.
functionality: Provides basic ballistic and acid-rain splash protection for the face; the polycarbonate strip offers partial eye shielding. No electronics, no seals — just mass between the wearer's face and the Shelf's hazards.
what_it_says: You build what you need from what's left, and you don't apologize for it.
story_hooks: A specific rivet pattern on one shield matches the stamp of a Crucible fab-floor press reported stolen three years ago — the trail leads somewhere uncomfortable.
A Shelf fixer uses an identical shield as a calling card; when one turns up on a body in Circuit, it means the fixer left it as a message.
A collector in Tier 4 is paying well over market for 'authentic Shelf ironwork' — the buyers don't know what they're funding.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, handcrafted face shield that reads as post-apocalyptic armor. Angular and asymmetrical, with overlapping steel panels creating a jagged, almost crown-like silhouette when viewed from above. Visually aggressive but functionally protective—appears worn by someone who prioritizes survival over aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Loose, adjustable fit secured by variable chin straps. Sits proud on the face with minimal contouring to skull anatomy. Forehead brace creates a rigid contact point; cheek and jaw coverage varies depending on panel overlap. Slightly oversized to accommodate layering or augmentation hardware underneath.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged industrial press plates (mild steel), mismatched rivet stock, polycarbonate sheet (transit shelter salvage), reclaimed foam padding, friction tape, knotted paracord or stripped copper wire
physical_description.texture: Heavily weathered and tactile—hammered steel with visible tool marks, acid-rain pitting creating a deeply pocked surface, rust bloom in corners and seams, scratched and clouded polycarbonate visor with micro-fractures, friction tape worn smooth in high-contact areas
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant grey-steel with rust-orange oxidation blooming across rivet heads and panel edges. Patchy darkening from acid rain exposure. Clear-to-amber polycarbonate visor with internal hazing and mineral deposits. Charcoal friction tape at forehead brace.
physical_description.closures: Knotted paracord or stripped wire chin straps (maker's choice), friction-fit panels held by mismatched rivet heads, no magnetic or electronic systems
distinctive_features: Hand-hammered panel seams with visible overlap
Mismatched rivet heads creating irregular surface texture
Acid-rain pitting across all steel surfaces
Scratched polycarbonate visor strip with internal clouding
No two shields identical—maker's individual variations visible
Chin strap knotted or twisted, often asymmetrical
Rust-orange oxidation patina, especially around fasteners
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 — sub-grade/ungoverned. This is pure salvage-tier aesthetics. Zero corporate finish, zero mass production. Signals someone operating outside formal economy.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Shelf dwellers, scrappers, autonomous-zone workers, and those in ungoverned districts. Indicates self-reliance, rejection of corpo supply chains, and comfort with DIY augmentation culture. Signals toughness and practical necessity over style—but also craftsmanship pride within constraints.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered and patched. Visor typically clouded and micro-scratched from use. Friction tape fraying at edges. Rust actively blooming in seams. Looks like it's been through seasons of acid rain and daily impact. Chinstrap often re-knotted or spliced with additional cord.

image_prompt: Close-up fashion shot of a Slagside Rivet-Crown Face Shield mounted on a dark industrial mannequin head, three-quarter view. Emphasize the hammered steel texture, acid-rain pitting, and overlapping mismatched panels. Polycarbonate visor catches moody violet-amber neon glow reflected from rain-slick urban backdrop. Harsh side-lighting reveals every tool mark and rivet head. Background: blurred GLMZ skyline at night, water-stained concrete underpass, faint holographic graffiti. Gritty, tactile, survival-focused.
